request.spec:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures now include the two new breakdowns, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

- **Per grade (A, B, C):** the due-totals of the people on that grade, added up over the sheet and all the sheets below it. Retired people are left out.
- **Per status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED, VOID, REVIEW):** the number of claims in that status over the same set of sheets.

Each sheet's figures are worked out the same way as its own Summary, then added up across the tree. A person whose due-total is n/a counts as zero here, as it does in the Summary. The new figures follow the screen's as-of date, like the existing consolidated figures.

This was a front-end change only; the server and stored data didn't need touching. The changes are in two files:
- `features/consolidated/consolidated.ts` now works out each sheet's per-grade due-totals and per-status claim counts alongside its existing figures.
- `features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx` adds them up over the tree and shows them with the test ids the spec expects (`consolidated-grade-<G>-due-total` and `consolidated-status-<S>-count`).

The header uses the same figures code but only reads the due-total and overdue-total, so it is unchanged.
